routes.label: List the common multiples in range

question: How many of the first one hundred positive integers are divisible by all of the numbers \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) \(5?\)
solution:
A number divisible by \(4\) is already divisible by \(2\), so we only need to impose divisibility by \(3,4,5\). The least common multiple of \(4\) and \(5\) is \(20\). Hence their common multiples among the first hundred positive integers are exactly
\[
20,40,60,80,100.
\]
Only \(60\) is also divisible by \(3\). Thus exactly \(1\) integer satisfies all four divisibility conditions, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
